change: Every login gets a session id (sid) shared by its access and refresh token. Logout revokes the session, so the refresh token dies too. A refresh token now works once (rotation: the used token is revoked, the new pair keeps the same sid); presenting a used token revokes the whole session. Change password sets forceLogoutAt (all older tokens stop working) and returns a fresh token pair so this PC keeps working.
tests: a refresh token that was already used (or logged out) is rejected; changePassword ends the user's other sessions; + 8 new scenario tests in tests/unit/auth/session-revocation.spec.ts
result: Before: 11 of 65 auth tests failed. After: 164 of 164 auth tests pass. Phases 1-8 re-run: no new failures (phase 1 now 238 tests, 1 failed = ES-393)

change: adminChangeUserPassword and updateUser (with a password) now set forceLogoutAt, truncated to the second, so every token of the target user issued before the reset stops working. A refused reset (target is an administrator or yourself) changes nothing.

result: Before: 3 of 3 session tests failed. After: all pass. Phase 2 now 405 tests, 51 failed (was 402 / 52); phases 1,3-8 unchanged
